definition: recursion depth = longest child-edge path from the query attributes into their descendant closure; only queries with depth>=3 are kept
source_queries: 48 of the 1234 queries in work/dag-scope/workload-run1/queries.tsv already have depth>=3; they are kept with their original SIFT test[qi] vectors
constructed: 252 further queries were built from the 37 depth>=3 attributes, adding partner attributes so each closure lands in a target nonempty-attribute bucket and |U| covers 1-4; vectors use SIFT test[1234+j]
regeneration: queries.tsv = first column |U| then attributes; queries.bin row j = test[vec_src]; gt_10.txt computed by exact FP32 top-10 over the closure
caveats: Depth is structural: empty intermediate attributes count as recursion levels but contribute no objects.
Same predicate may recur with a different query vector; each vector is a distinct query.
Only 37 attributes reach depth>=3, so buckets 2 and 3-5 reuse few scopes with different vectors.
